ca_northwest_california.blurb: Northwest California is a spread-out collection of crags. Sport routes dominate, with some bouldering, a modest amount of trad and a few top-ropes. Roped grades mostly run from 5.10 to 5.12, with a handful of 5.13s and a thin base of easier climbs. Lover's Leap, a limestone plug on a ridge in the Scott Valley area, is the largest single crag, with mostly sport lines on rock described as good to excellent; spring and fall are generally best there, and its walls face different ways so sun or shade is usually available. Russian Wilderness and Crescent City Area also hold climbs.

ca_west_side.blurb: The West Side is the part of Pinnacles National Park, on California's Central Coast, where the longer routes are found. The park's rock is volcanic breccia, which can be loose in places, and the climbing has an adventurous feel. Most lines here are multi-pitch and easier face climbs, with moderate single pitches on formations such as Flumes Formation and longer two- to seven-pitch lines on The Balconies and Machete Ridge. Trad and sport are both common, with some top-rope and a small bouldering rock. Grades run from about 5.4 to 5.12 and bunch up between 5.6 and 5.10. Many multi-pitch lines have a reputation for loose rock, though nearly all have been re-bolted.

co_access_fund_trailhead_the.blurb: These cliffs lie in Unaweep Canyon south of Grand Junction, Colorado, where the walls are long, steep granite rising several hundred feet. Traditional climbing leads by a wide margin, with a smaller set of sport routes. Grades run from about 5.6 to 5.13 and stack up between 5.10 and 5.11, with a solid group of 5.8 and 5.9 lines. Sunday Wall is the most visited crag, with solid rock overall, some loose sections, and routes up to five pitches from 5.6 to 5.12. Hidden Valley Wall, Television Wall and Fortress Wall sit nearby. In the canyon as a whole, spring and fall are best, and since it runs east to west you can chase sun in cool months and shade in summer.

nm_gallup_area.blurb: Climbing around Gallup, in western New Mexico, is on sandstone. Mentmore, the main crag, is an uplifted shelf of tan Cretaceous sandstone with single-pitch sport routes and a few trad lines, mostly moderate. The sandstone is fragile when wet, and July and August are the rainy season. The area can be climbed year-round, and winter days are warm in the sun. Crowds are rare. Bouldering is the other draw: the Barn Yard holds about two dozen easy to moderate problems beneath the Gallup Hogback, and Todd's Boulders adds more. Across the area, sport is the largest share, grades mostly sit between 5.9 and 5.11, and boulder problems range from easy through the V6 range.

oh_raven_rocks.blurb: Raven Rocks is a scenic bouldering area in Eastern Ohio, a region on the edge of Appalachia whose boulders are sandstone. Every problem here is a boulder problem, from V0 through the V10 range, with the bulk falling between V2 and V7. Night Moves is the biggest of the four main zones, alongside The Point, Pine Ridge and North Gorge. Pine Ridge sits on a ridge in pine forest and has some of the harder problems, on rock described as the best quality around. Several smaller boulder groups require off-trail navigation and are hard to reach in summer. The scenery is often compared to Hocking Hills.

wy_lower_canyon_granite.blurb: Lower Canyon Granite sits at the bottom of Shoshone Canyon beside the river, a few miles west of Cody, Wyoming. The rock is granite that is fractured and heavily featured, with friction that depends on conditions. Sport climbing is the majority, with a solid share of trad and some mixed lines. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.13 and concentrate between 5.10 and 5.12, with a small group of 5.13s. Walls on the north side above the road get good sun, while the south wall across the river is cooler. Spring and fall are best on nice days, and summer is comfortable for most of the season. The Single Malt Wall, Riverside Wall and Lower Vegas Wall are among the larger groupings.
